The applicable subheading for Semi-Finished Good B will be 2825.90.9000, Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), which provides for Hydrazine and hydroxylamine and their inorganic salts; other inorganic bases; other metal oxides, hydroxides and peroxides: Other: Other. The general rate of duty will be 3.7 percent ad valorem. [...] Description of Goods: Semi-Finished Good A, B and C

Semi-Finished Good A (precursor) is nickel cobalt manganese hydroxide in a black powder state, which is manufactured by reacting four different raw materials (nickel sulfate, cobalt sulfate, manganese sulfate, sodium hydroxide) under a special manufacturing process. The result is a metal hydroxide composed of three metallic elements, which is also called a “precursor” in the commercial market. [...] The applicable subheading for the Finished Good will be 3824.99.3900, HTSUS, which provides for Prepared binders for foundry molds or cores; chemical products and preparations of the chemical or allied industries (including those consisting of mixtures of natural products), not elsewhere specified or included: Other: Other: Other: Mixtures of two or more inorganic compounds: Other. The general rate of duty will be free.

results.content:
took on heightened importance beginning in 2018, when the first Trump Administration imposed additional tariffs of 25% on Chinese lithium ion battery parts while imposing lower additional duties of 7.5% on Chinese lithium ion batteries. [...] The U.S. Customs & Border Protection (CBP) published a Notice that would revoke the Agency’s previous rulings on lithium ion cells in favor of classifying cells in the U.S. harmonized tariff schedule (HTS) applicable to batteries. Until 2018, the CBP’s tariff classification position on cells and batteries was of little practical importance because there was no difference in the duties applicable to imports under any of the applicable codes. However, the CBP’s stance took on heightened [...] CBP’s ruling revocations generally become effective 60 days after publication of the final revocation Notice. However, consistent with its general practice regarding ruling revocations, CBP has not identified a specific date for final adoption of its new proposal. Rather, the timeline will likely depend on the number and scope of comments received.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the US tariff on lithium-ion batteries?

Lithium-ion batteries are classified under HTS 8507.60 with a base duty rate of 3.4%. Section 301 tariffs on Chinese-origin lithium-ion batteries add 25%, bringing the effective rate to 28.4% for Chinese imports.
